description: An independent study course, the nature and content of which is agreed upon between the individual and the person offering the course. Subject to the approval of the student's advisory committee and the graduate program committee.
departments: School of Theatre, English, and Creative Writing

title: Reading Course II
description: An independent study course, the nature and content of which is agreed upon between the individual and the person offering the course. Subject to the approval of the student's advisory committee and the graduate program committee.
departments: School of Theatre, English, and Creative Writing

title: Qualitative Research Methods
description: This course examines qualitative research methods used in food, tourism, and sport, as well as related hospitality and service management areas. Topics include types of qualitative methods, their theoretical foundations, project design, data collection, and analysis procedures and strategies, as well as appropriate communication of results.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Foundations of Tourism and Hospitality
description: The course is designed to discuss theoretical concepts and theories which provide an understanding of societal, managerial and strategic aspects of tourism and hospitality. An emphasis will also be placed on key theories and concepts of relevant disciplines which may affect tourism and hospitality research.
restrictions: Restricted to Tourism Research Graduate Diploma, Tourism and Hospitality MSc and Management PhD students.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Foundations of Food Industry Management
description: This course introduces students to the theories and practices of the food industry, including global and regional food system, with an examination of food policies that frame supply chains. Students discuss topics that influence food systems such as ethics, supply chains, food product marketing, consumer choice, food literacy, and the food service sector.
restrictions: Restricted to Tourism and Hospitality MSc students.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Contemporary Issues in Tourism
description: The course will acquaint students with the tourism industry. An overview of the scale and scope, involved stakeholders,and the organization of the industry will be examined and critiqued. An emphasis will be placed on the sustainable development and management of tourism resources and organizations.
restrictions: Restricted to Tourism Research Graduate Diploma, Tourism and Hospitality MSc and Management PhD students.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Hospitality and Tourism Revenue Management
description: This course is an advanced exploration of revenue management concepts, tools and application. The objective of the course is to provide a solid foundation in revenue management for careers in tourism, services and hospitality management. Offered in conjunction with HTM*4250 . Extra work is required for graduate students.
restrictions: Credit may only be obtained for one of TRMH*6240 or HTM*4250 .

title: Tourism and Sustainable Development
description: The course introduces students to the issues affecting planning and development of tourism by understanding tourism planning and sustainable development. Core elements include a discussion on tourism impacts (economic, social, cultural and environmental), issues of sustainability, carrying capacity, 'eco-tourism' and other 'alternative forms' of tourism.
restrictions: Restricted to Graduate Diploma Tourism Research, MSc Tourism and Hospitality and PhD Management students.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Data Mining Practicum
description: An applied course introducing popular concepts, methods and applications of data mining utilizing data warehoused at the government agencies and user friendly software and cases. This course covers various topics in data mining association rule, clustering, logistic regression, decision tree and artificial neural network.
restrictions: Restricted to Graduate Diploma Tourism Research, MSc Tourism and Hospitality.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Research Methods for Tourism and Hospitality
description: This course looks at selected analytical techniques in tourism and hospitality research, both empirical and subjective, as well the nature of research questions and theory. The course is intended to help students make informed judgements about selected research tools and designs, and draw logical and substantive conclusions.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Research Applications in Tourism and Hospitality
description: This course is designed to enhance the student's analytical capability, using both basic and advanced analytical techniques and tools of tourism and hospitality research. They learn to critically evaluate, enabling them to make effective judgments, choose proper statistical techniques, and draw logical and substantive conclusions.
prerequisites: TRMH*6100 and one of TRMH*6290 , MCS*6050 , SOC*6130 or PSYC*6060
restrictions: Restricted to Graduate Diploma Tourism Research, MSc Tourism and Hospitality and PhD Management students.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Thesis Research Proposal
description: The students engage in seminars to share experiences and reflections on the research process. This course is a development of the proposal: framing a research question, developing a methodological plan within a challenging interdisciplinary area such as tourism and hospitality, data planning and more.
restrictions: Restricted to MSc Tourism and Hospitality students in the thesis option.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Major Research Project
description: This course is available to individuals or groups of graduate students registered in MSc Tourism and Hospitality - MRP option. Students complete a set of readings and an associated paper as approved by designated faculty.
restrictions: Restricted to MSc Tourism and Hospitality students in the coursework/MRP option.

title: Special Topics in Tourism
description: Advanced course for those specializing in tourism. Deals with theories of tourism generators, multi-markets, tourism multipliers, current and future trends, regulatory environments, and distributions systems.
departments: School of Hospitality, Food and Tourism Management

title: Advanced Principles of Toxicology
description: An intensive course in the principles of modern aspects of toxicology, taught in a lecture/case study format.

title: Advanced Topics in Toxicology
description: Advanced topics in toxicology will include oral presentations by students, faculty members, and guest lecturers. The emphasis will be on advanced concepts and techniques in toxicology research with particular relevance to mechanistic, molecular and interpretive toxicology. Offered in conjunction with TOX*4200 . Extra work is required of graduate students.
restrictions: Credit may be obtained for only one of TOX*6200 or TOX*4200

title: Biochemical Toxicology
description: The molecular mechanisms of action of carcinogens and other toxic compounds. Enzymes of biotransformation, including a detailed study of cytochrome P-450. Interactions of reactive species with DNA and other macromolecules. Offered in conjunction with TOX*4590 . Extra work is required of graduate students.
restrictions: Credit may be obtained for only one of TOX*4590 and TOX*6590

title: Work Experience
description: This is a semester-long experience in a typically paid work setting designed for students to apply their theoretical knowledge in a vocational setting. In this course, students develop goals to be achieved during the semester and work with their employer to evaluate progress on achieving their goals. At the conclusion of the work experience, students will reflect on their experiences and how these may inform their future career goals. Students must obtain a passing work experience report evaluation and work performance evaluation grade from the employer to receive WEX Certification.
restrictions: Enrolment in a Work Experience (WEX) approved program.

title: Work Experience Preparation
description: Students acquire the skills required to succeed in a competitive employment process as part of the Work Experience Program (WEX). The course covers how to identify and communicate skills, knowledge and abilities, how to write an effective resume and cover letter and learn about specific interview techniques. This course also introduces students to theory, practice and policies of WEX to prepare them for the WEX employment process. Students complete this course as a prerequisite to the Work Experience Employment Process Course WEX*6110 .
restrictions: Enrolment in a Work Experience (WEX) approved program.
offering: Offered through Distance Education format only

title: Work Experience Employment Process
description: Students learn about the Work Experience (WEX) employment cycle and obtain practice and support in applying to WEX roles on the Experience Guelph site. Students prepare for interviews and develop their professional brand to match their knowledge of self with employer needs. This course discusses legislation, roles and responsibilities for maintaining employee health and safety and well-being, including related responsibilities of employers and the rights of employees. In addition, students self-reflect regarding career development and what is required to be successful in a professional hiring process and work setting.
restrictions: Enrolment in a Work Experience (WEX) approved program.
offering: Offered through Distance Education format only
